subject: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme-health.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@acme-health.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can move into a short eval/canary: 

Goals we heard
- Real-time clinical note generation at rounding speed (streaming output)
- High coherence on partial/early tokens (avoid jagged/incoherent partials)
- Support for stop sequences tied to embedded templates
- Target latency: 150–300ms per token at 4 concurrent streams

Current pain points you mentioned
- Partial outputs occasionally truncate mid-sentence on streaming clients
- Stop sequences sometimes not honored when the model switches variants
- Recent switch to a newer model showed a drop in multi-turn coherence in our internal evals

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) You share current benchmark CSV + prompt set (you mentioned you would).
2) We run a quick model-fit evaluation across 2–3 candidate models and return an eval summary + recommended canary config (A/B with fallback).
3) Short technical demo (30m) to walk through streaming behavior, stop sequence options, and canary rollout.

I'll assemble an eval plan and recommended models once we have your benchmark and prompt set — target delivery by early next week.

Attachments: none from our side yet — please send over your benchmarks/prompts when convenient.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Growth — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@acme-health.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Sending our sample benchmark and the prompt set we use in production (attached). A few notes up front from our side: 

- Attached: benchmark_results.csv (latency & per-turn quality metrics), prompt_set_v1.json (canonical prompts)
- We observed a quality regression after moving from redwood-v1 to redwood-v2 in streaming mode: partial outputs can be less coherent in the first 8–12 tokens for multi-turn prompts.
- Stop sequences are critical for our templated notes — when the model variant changes we sometimes see the stop token not respected.

Can you confirm which models you plan to evaluate? We prefer something that maintains parity with our current redwood-v1 behavior for streaming but gives overall better cost/perf. Also can you outline the canary/fallback approach and whether we can limit the canary to a single region?

Happy to do the 30m demo next week — mornings PST are best.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Product, Clinical NLP — ACME Health
emily.zhao@acme-health.com

Attachments: benchmark_results.csv, prompt_set_v1.json

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Thanks Emily — got the files and great notes. Initial plan and recommendations: 

Recommended candidate models to evaluate (shortlist)
- redwood-v2-medium: best quality/latency balance (recommended primary canary)
- redwood-v1-small: lower-cost baseline that matches your current behavior (recommended fallback)
- redwood-quantized-fast: experimental, for throughput testing if you want to try aggressive quantization

What we'll deliver
- A/B canary config doc with rollout fraction, region scoping, and automatic fallback to redwood-v1-small on quality regressions.
- Per-prompt eval comparing token-level perplexity, stop-sequence adherence rates, and streaming coherence metrics.
- A short recording of streaming sessions showing partial output behavior (so your engineers can inspect).

Links
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-HP-42
- Model catalog + benchmark page: https://redwood-inference.com/models/redwood-v2-benchmarks
- Shared folder (will drop eval artifacts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_link

Proposed timeline
- Mar 2: short demo (30m) and agree on canary fraction/region
- Mar 3–5: run A/B canary and gather eval metrics
- Mar 6: deliver eval summary and recommended rollout plan

Please confirm a demo slot (mornings PST preferred). We'll include an engineer (Jordan) and solutions lead (Vivek).

Best,
Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Quick technical note from our engineering side on the streaming coherence / stop-sequence issues you described. High-level observations and things we'll instrument during the canary: 

1) Partial output coherence
- In streaming mode, early-token coherence can degrade when the model receives differing system/context framing across requests (e.g., subtle prompt tokenization changes). We'll compare tokenization alignment and prefix cache behavior between redwood-v1 and redwood-v2.

2) Stop sequences not honored
- In a small subset of sessions we saw stop tokens arrive one or two tokens late when a fallback trigger occurred mid-stream. We'll add deterministic stop handling in the endpoint (post-process token stream to enforce stop sequence once emitted) and compare adherence rate.

3) Latency/throughput
- We can configure batching and KV-cache lifetimes per route. For your target (150–300ms/token at 4 streams) we'll start with continuous batching disabled for the canary to keep latency predictable and set burst capacity to 6 concurrent requests.

Action items from engineering
- We'll collect sample streaming traces and share streaming_sample.log (attached) showing token timestamps and stop-token events.
- Implement canary policy that routes 10% of traffic to redwood-v2-medium in us-west1 with automatic rollback to redwood-v1-small on any stop-sequence regression >2% or token-coherence regression >3% measured on your prompt set.

Attaching: streaming_sample.log (small, redacted)

—Jordan
Principal Engineer, Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme-health.com>

Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Thanks Jordan & team — that plan sounds good. A couple of clarifications: 

- We did see the regressions primarily on multi-turn templates where the system message plus last user turn produce a short answer followed by a stop token. The partial output sometimes contains extra punctuation or truncated phrases in the first 10 tokens.
- Can you confirm the exact rollback trigger metrics and whether those thresholds can be tuned after we start the canary?
- We'll want the canary scoped to us-west1 only initially. If things look good, we'll expand to other regions.

Yes to a 30m technical demo — mornings PST are great. Can we do Wed Mar 4 at 10:00am PST? Also please include suggested agenda points for the demo (short).

Emily

3) Deliver full eval report by Mar 6.

Attaching the artifacts we discussed after the canary: benchmark_results.csv, prompt_set_v1.json, streaming_sample.log (already shared).
